Danish Energy Agency and Energinet (2026). Technology Data - Heating installations (Technology Data for Heating Installations), version 0007, April 2026. Copenhagen: Danish Energy Agency. ISBN 978-87-94447-49-2. www.ens.dk/technologydata. Data sheets: technology_data_heating_installations - 07.xlsx.
All costs are real 2025 EUR excluding VAT and taxes (p.11 and p.14; Index sheet: "All cost data is in 2025 EURO"); Danish data converted at 7.46 DKK/EUR by the source.

Scope: only apartment-complex (larger, ~100-500 kW) units that could serve industrial space heating were extracted: oil boiler (201, existing = mineral oil, new = bio-oil), condensing gas boiler (202), automatic-stoking biomass boiler (204), air-to-water and ground-source heat pumps (207), electric boiler (209) and electric panel heating (216, new building only), each for existing and new buildings as separate examples (13 examples, 8 technology names). Not extracted: single-family sheets (residential), district-heating substations 203 (no archetype), manual biomass boiler and wood stoves (single-family only), air-to-air and ventilation heat pumps, solar heating 215. Values come from the alldata_flat sheet: 2025 central as value, 2025 lower/upper as min/max. Capex and fixed O&M are printed per unit (k EUR/unit, EUR/unit/yr); converted to per kW of heat output by dividing by the central unit capacity (formula column), since the catalogue says its bounds are cost uncertainty for the standard unit, not a size range. Efficiencies are annual-average net heat efficiency at LHV, incl. DHW tank losses, excl. auxiliary electricity; for heat pumps the SPF. CH4/N2O are g per GJ fuel input (LHV). CO2 not given. Units are whole heating systems for a building incl. hot tap water. 2030-2050 values in _projections.csv; auxiliary electricity (kWh/yr), equipment/installation split, the separate "additional" investment, floor-heating SPF, NOx/SO2/PM2.5, demand shares and manual O&M hours in _other-values.csv. Locator convention: printed page numbers equal PDF page numbers ("Page N | 99" header); data rows cite the workbook sheet.
